title: Agent skill + Claude/Codex marketplace integration
description:
Outcome: a tiny agent skill that teaches Claude Code and Codex agents to use hunch well, installable from this repo as a Claude Code plugin marketplace. Lead-added bead (Thomas, 2026-09-19): "create a bead for an associated claude/codex skill with marketplace integration. Keep it super simple and lightweight."

Scope (minimal):
- `skills/hunch/SKILL.md`: frontmatter `name` + `description` (when to use: pointing at a line/file/tool/hunk, root-causing a failing command, yes/no predicates on text). Body under ~60 lines: install check (`hunch health`), the verbs with one example each, always use `--json` and read `exit_code` (0 ok, 1 no, 3 abstain = treat as "nothing fits", 4/5/6 errors), `hunch capabilities --json` and `hunch robot-docs guide` as the source of truth, safety (`run --dry-run` by default; never `--exec --yes` without the user's say-so; `add --dry-run` first). Facts only from README, docs/ROBOT_MODE.md, docs/guide/, `capabilities`.
- Claude Code marketplace: `.claude-plugin/marketplace.json` at repo root listing one plugin `hunch` whose source is this repo, plus the plugin manifest (`.claude-plugin/plugin.json` or the layout the current docs require) exposing `skills/`. Verify the exact schema against current Claude Code plugin/marketplace docs (use the claude-code-guide agent or https://docs.claude.com) before writing; no guessing.
- Codex: document in the README "Agents" section how to use the same SKILL.md with Codex (copy/symlink into the Codex skills directory, per current Codex docs — verify), one short paragraph. No extra files unless Codex requires one.
- README: 3–5 lines in "Agents": `/plugin marketplace add tpellet/hunch` then `/plugin install hunch@<marketplace-name>` (exact syntax verified), and the Codex note.

Out of scope: hooks, commands, MCP servers, scripts. Use the current name `hunch` (a rename to `judge` is planned separately).

Validation: if `claude plugin validate` (or the documented validator) exists, run it and record the result; JSON files parse (`jq .`). Gate: cargo fmt --check and cargo test --locked -- --test-threads=1 still green; ubs "not applicable — nothing scanned" for Markdown/JSON.

Rules: RULE ZERO (no rm in any form, no deletion, no prompts, no redirects to variable paths); shared checkout under Agent Mail (register as worker-sk, reserve your paths + .beads/issues.jsonl, thread = this bead ID, report to lead-0); CI pre-check, claim, work; one signed commit `feat: agent skill and plugin marketplace (<this-id>)`; no Co-Authored-By or Claude-Session trailer; pre-push gitleaks + diff read; push; CI green for your SHA; close with evidence.

title: classifier.dev fallback when there is no TypeSafe key
description:
Outcome: grevi works with no TypeSafe key, by using classifier.dev as a second backend. Lead-added bead (Thomas, 2026-09-19): "have an additional bead to have classifier dev as an alternative API if you don't have a typesafe api key".

KEY FACT from Thomas (2026-09-19, supersedes any guess): classifier.dev runs Jev behind the scenes and serves it for free. So the features should be at full parity, not a degraded mode. Design for parity and prove it; do not write caveat copy about a weaker fallback unless a measurement forces you to.

What Thomas gave us: "Zero-shot text classification over plain HTTP. You send text and a list of labels, you get back the label that fits and how sure the model is. There is no API key or account required for free use... the OpenAPI 3.1 description is at https://classifier.dev/openapi.json and a short index at https://classifier.dev/llms.txt".

Step 1 - research before code (record findings in the bead notes):
- Read https://classifier.dev/llms.txt and https://classifier.dev/openapi.json (curl, sandbox disabled). Establish: endpoints, request and response shape, label limit, text size limit, rate limits, latency, whether it returns the same probabilities as Jev, and the terms of use for a client like grevi.
- Map grevi's two question kinds onto it: "which one" (choice over options plus NONE) and "is it" (absolute yes/no with a probability). Since the model is the same, the work is the wire format, not the semantics. If a shape is missing (NONE, absolute yes/no, batching, the 200-option window), say so plainly and name the workaround.
- Verify parity, do not assume it: run the existing evals (scripts/eval_run.py, scripts/eval_why.py) against both backends and record the two numbers side by side. Equal numbers are the expected result and the evidence we publish. A real gap is a finding: report it before writing any copy about it.

Step 2 - implementation (small, behind the existing client seam):
- A backend chosen by config: TypeSafe Jev when a key is present, classifier.dev when none is. GREVI_BACKEND=typesafe|classifier forces either. No key, no prompt, no signup path.
- Reuse the existing cache, retry, timeout and error mapping. Keep exit codes and the JSON envelope identical. meta reports which backend and model answered.
- health reports the active backend. capabilities lists the new env var and the backend field.
- Respect the free service: honour its rate limits, set a clear user agent (grevi/<version>), and keep concurrency conservative by default.
- Tests: contract tests with a wiremock fake for the new backend (no live network in the default run), plus one #[ignore] live test.
- Docs: README (a short "No key needed" paragraph - grevi runs out of the box, a TypeSafe key gets you your own quota), docs/guide/configuration.md and faq.md, PRIVACY.md (with this backend the text goes to classifier.dev instead of TypeSafe).

Out of scope: a local model, other providers, changing the threshold semantics, any change to the Jev path's behaviour.

Gate and rules: full gate (fmt, check, clippy -D warnings, tests, doc, cargo deny, ubs exit 0 on changed code) plus the live checks above; RULE ZERO (no rm in any form, no prompts, no redirects to variable paths); shared checkout under Agent Mail (register, reserve paths, thread = this bead ID, report to lead-0); CI pre-check, claim, work; signed commits; pre-push gitleaks and diff read; push; CI green.

Posting is Thomas's call; say so in the hand-off.
- Never delete files; treat unexplained working-tree changes as another agent's work: never stash, revert or overwrite them; commit only your own paths; `main` only, no branches. Start with the CI pre-check (the "Before claiming" step of the CI criterion in Done when: a read-only `gh run list`; a red previous run is fixed and pushed under the previous bead's ID before anything else); only then claim: `br update hunch-launch-tweet-mtr --claim --actor worker-<short-id> --json` (pick a short id such as `worker-a1`; use the same `--actor` on every br command and name it in the close reason), then `br sync --flush-only`. `br` auto-flushes `.beads/issues.jsonl`; that file is the only file you stage — the claim and the close ride in this bead's one commit.

- [ ] Pre-push scan (every bead: the repo `tpellet/hunch` is public, so a push is publication; the rule is ~/.claude/AGENTS.md "## Public Repositories — Push With Care", this is the hunch form). Before every `git push`, outside the sandbox: `gitleaks git . --log-opts="origin/main..HEAD" --redact -v` (gitleaks 8.30.1 is installed; `brew install gitleaks` if it is missing; the repo's `.gitleaks.toml` allowlist, added by hunch-task-01-scaffold-p8n, is picked up automatically) must end with "no leaks found"; then read `git diff origin/main..HEAD` yourself for private information: API keys or tokens, `Authorization` headers, pasted API responses, emails other than the commit author's, absolute local paths (`/Users/...`, `/private/tmp/...`) anywhere but in bead and plan instructions, which already name the checkout and the launch folder by absolute path, scratchpad or session URLs, names of Thomas's private repos or projects, personal or admin details, other people's data, communications drafts (tweet, Show HN, announcement: those live only in /Users/tpellet/Projects/hunch-launch/, never in the repo, bead notes, close reasons or commit messages). State `pre-push scan: clean` in the hand-off.
- [ ] CI (one rule for every bead: a red run belongs to the bead whose push turned it red and is fixed under that bead's ID). Before claiming — the first step of this bead, read-only: `gh run list --workflow ci.yml --branch main --limit 3 --json databaseId,headSha,status,conclusion` (outside the sandbox) and use the run whose `headSha` equals `git rev-parse origin/main` (re-list after a few seconds if it is not there yet). title: Rename hunch to grevi everywhere
description:
Outcome: the project is `grevi` everywhere — crate, library, binary, env vars, cache dir, user agent, messages, tests, docs, skill, demo — and the renamed binary is proven to work live. Lead-added bead (Thomas, 2026-09-19: "renamed to grevi... refactor everything to grevi now... Make sure to test the rust binary to check it works").

Rename map (do all of it; `rg -n 'hunch|HUNCH|Hunch'` must come back empty except the exceptions below):
- `Cargo.toml`: `name = "grevi"`; keep `publish = false` for now (Thomas is creating his crates.io login; a publish is his call). Cargo.lock updated by cargo.

title: Rust best practices: tooling, tests, clean CI/CD
description:
Outcome: hunch follows current Rust tooling, testing and CI/CD best practice, so CI is clean, reproducible and easy to extend with GitHub Actions: a pinned toolchain file, an MSRV check, locked builds, rustdoc and dependency-audit checks, cached and least-privilege workflows, dependency update automation and complete Cargo metadata. Lead-added bead (Thomas, 2026-09-19): "verify that we follow Rust best practices when it comes to tooling/testing etc. so that we have clean CI/CD and can easily integrate with GitHub Actions if needed." Not in the original plan; this bead is its spec.

Read first: ~/.claude/AGENTS.md and /Users/tpellet/Projects/hunch/AGENTS.md (every time); Cargo.toml, .github/workflows/ci.yml, .gitignore, .gitleaks.toml, the plan's "## Global Constraints" and Task 16 (cargo-dist owns the release workflow, which Task 16 generates AFTER this bead: do not create release.yml here). Verify every third-party action, tool and config key against its current primary docs before use (GitHub docs, the action's README, docs.rs, the cargo book); record the URLs you checked in the close reason.

Context:
- Before claiming: run the CI pre-check (the "Before claiming" step of the CI criterion in Done when); only then claim: `br update <this-id> --claim --actor worker-<short-id> --json`.
- Audit first, then change. Write a short checklist in the bead notes (`br update --append-notes`): each item below as PASS (already true, with evidence) / FIXED (what changed) / SKIPPED (why). Do not churn what is already right.
- Checklist:
  1. Toolchain: add `rust-toolchain.toml` pinning the same toolchain CI uses (1.93.1, components rustfmt and clippy) so local and CI match; CI keeps `dtolnay/rust-toolchain` at the same version.
  2. MSRV: a CI job (ubuntu only) that runs `cargo check --locked --all-targets` on the declared `rust-version` (1.87) so the floor is real; if it fails, report it — do not raise `rust-version` silently; fixing the MSRV is a finding for the lead.
  3. Locked, reproducible builds: `Cargo.lock` committed (it is a binary); CI uses `--locked` on check/clippy/test; `cargo fmt --all --check`.
  4. Tests: `cargo test --locked --all-targets -- --test-threads=1` plus `cargo test --locked --doc`; live tests stay `#[ignore]` and never run in CI (no secrets in CI); no network in default tests.
  5. Docs: `RUSTDOCFLAGS="-D warnings" cargo doc --locked --no-deps` passes (fix broken intra-doc links in place if any).
  6. Supply chain: add `cargo-deny` with a minimal `deny.toml` (advisories, licenses allow-list covering the current dependency tree as MIT-compatible for this MIT project, bans duplicates as warn, sources crates.io only) and a CI job using the official `EmbarkStudios/cargo-deny-action`; run `cargo deny check` locally first (install with `cargo install cargo-deny --locked`, outside the sandbox). A real advisory is a finding: fix by `cargo update -p <crate>` if a patched version exists, else record and report.
  7. Workflow hygiene: `permissions: contents: read` at the top; `concurrency` group with `cancel-in-progress: true` for PR/branch runs; `Swatinem/rust-cache` for build caching; `actions/checkout` on its current major (the Node 20 deprecation annotation seen on CI run 35445297521 must disappear); job `timeout-minutes`; matrix stays ubuntu-latest + macos-latest. Validate with `actionlint` (`brew install actionlint`, outside the sandbox) — exit 0.
  8. Dependency automation: `.github/dependabot.yml` for `cargo` and `github-actions`, weekly, grouped minor/patch.
  9. Cargo metadata: `description`, `license = "MIT"`, `repository`, `homepage` (repo URL), `readme`, `keywords` (≤5), `categories` (valid crates.io slugs, e.g. command-line-utilities), `rust-version`; keep `publish = false` (crates.io name taken) and the cargo-dist `dist = true` rule for Task 16 intact. Optional `[profile.release]` `lto = "thin"`, `codegen-units = 1`, `strip = true` ONLY with a measured before/after of binary size and `hunch --version` wall time (AGENTS.md: no performance claim without a baseline); otherwise SKIPPED.
  10. Lints: a `[lints.rust]` table with `unsafe_code = "forbid"` is equivalent to the crate attribute; add it only if it does not conflict with the tests' permitted `unsafe { set_var }` (tests/ are separate crates — check); otherwise SKIPPED with the reason.
  11. README: a CI status badge at the top, linking to the ci.yml workflow (one line; keep Thomas's voice rules from 13b/13d for any prose).
- Never weaken a gate: no `continue-on-error`, no dropped platforms, no `#[ignore]`/deleted tests, no clippy allows to get green.
- Files: Create: rust-toolchain.toml, deny.toml, .github/dependabot.yml. Modify: .github/workflows/ci.yml, Cargo.toml, README.md (badge only), and source files only to fix rustdoc -D warnings findings. Do not touch src logic, the plan's verified code or release.yml.
- AFK RULE: never run any command that needs a human confirmation or that dcg blocks (rm, rm -rf, git reset --hard, git clean, git stash, git checkout -- <path>, force-push, mv over an existing file, redirects to variable paths); skip, record with --append-notes, continue.

Done when:
- [ ] Checklist items 1–11 recorded in notes as PASS / FIXED / SKIPPED with evidence.
- [ ] Local gate with the sandbox disabled: `cargo fmt --all --check`, `cargo check --locked --all-targets`, `cargo clippy --locked --all-targets -- -D warnings`, `cargo test --locked -- --test-threads=1`, `cargo test --locked --doc`, `RUSTDOCFLAGS="-D warnings" cargo doc --locked --no-deps`, `cargo deny check`, `actionlint` — all exit 0. `ubs` on changed code files exit 0, or "ubs: not applicable — nothing scanned (exit 3)" when only non-code changed; never an override.
- [ ] One signed commit `chore: harden CI and Rust tooling (<this-id>)` staging exactly the files above plus `.beads/issues.jsonl` (claim and close ride in it; `br close` then `br sync --flush-only` before committing). No Co-Authored-By, no Claude-Session trailer.
- [ ] Pre-push scan: `gitleaks git . --log-opts="origin/main..HEAD" --redact -v` no leaks, and read `git diff origin/main..HEAD` for keys, tokens, absolute local paths in user-facing files, emails, session URLs, personal details; on a hit fix forward, never rewrite history. Global rule: ~/.claude/AGENTS.md "Public Repositories — Push With Care".
- [ ] CI (outside the sandbox): Before claiming, `gh run list --workflow ci.yml --branch main --limit 3 --json databaseId,headSha,status,conclusion` and match `headSha` to `git rev-parse origin/main`; wait for it; a red run belongs to the bead whose push turned it red. After your push, match your `HEAD` SHA, `gh run watch <databaseId>`, and every job (including the new MSRV and cargo-deny jobs) must be green with no deprecation annotations; a red run is yours to fix under this bead ID (`fix: <what ≤22 chars> (<this-id>)`, note appended with br before the fix commit). Release-workflow (tag) runs belong to the acceptance bead.
acceptance_criteria: Checklist 1-11 recorded; local gate incl. --locked tests, doc -D warnings, cargo deny, actionlint all exit 0; signed commit pushed; every CI job incl. MSRV and cargo-deny green with no deprecation annotations.
notes: Checklist: 1 toolchain FIXED (rust-toolchain.toml 1.93.1); 2 MSRV FIXED (CI job on 1.87.0); 3 --locked FIXED; 4 tests FIXED (--locked, doc tests); 5 docs FIXED (one rustdoc invalid_html_tags on Sort::into allowed, --help unchanged); 6 cargo-deny FIXED (all ok; CDLA-Permissive-2.0 allowed for webpki-root-certs); 7 workflow hygiene FIXED (permissions read, concurrency, checkout v7, rust-cache v2, timeouts; actionlint 0); 8 dependabot FIXED; 9 metadata FIXED (release profile pre-existing from bead 01); 10 lints table SKIPPED (would forbid unsafe set_var in tests); 11 badge deferred to 13b integration (README owned by 13b).
close_reason: Integrated by lead from parallel worktree wt/bead-rust (Sonnet worker b5d7131). Local gate on main: fmt --all, clippy --locked -D warnings, 66 tests --locked, rustdoc -D warnings, cargo deny (advisories/bans/licenses/sources ok), actionlint 0 — all green. CI with new msrv/docs/cargo-deny jobs checked after push. Dependency rewired 13d -> 12 for the parallel run.

title: Secret, private-info and PII audit before release
description:
Outcome: Before v0 is tagged and released, the public repo `tpellet/hunch` is audited end to end for secrets, private information and PII: a full-history gitleaks scan, a manual review of every tracked file and of the commit history, a check that no launch draft lives in the repo, a check that the release config and the locally built installer carry no local paths, and a check that user-facing docs use the generic key path and no personal tooling details. Fix-forward findings are fixed in this bead; anything that would need a history rewrite or a key rotation is recorded, never rewritten, and blocks v0 acceptance pending Thomas. The verdict is a short pass/fail note in the close reason with no secret value quoted. Lead-added (Thomas, 2026-09-19: "before the push to public remote we check for any secret/any private information and PII that should not be shared"); the lead's own audit of the pre-code history (2026-09-19) found SECRET 0, and the lead's authorized history rewrite of 2026-09-19 removed the low PRIVATE items, so the pre-code baseline is clean (17 commits at 5ed92d6).

Read first: ~/.claude/AGENTS.md ("## Public Repositories — Push With Care") and /Users/tpellet/Projects/hunch/AGENTS.md (every time); the plan docs/superpowers/plans/2026-09-18-hunch-v0.md — "## Global Constraints" and "### Task 16: Release — binaries, launch checklist (Homebrew tap and Show HN optional, user-gated)" Step 2b; `.gitleaks.toml` (hunch-task-01-scaffold-p8n); README.md, PRIVACY.md, docs/ROBOT_MODE.md, CHANGELOG.md, benchmarks/results.md as shipped.

Context:
- Scope: everything reachable from `git log --all` plus every tracked file at HEAD (`git ls-files`), including `.beads/issues.jsonl` (descriptions, notes, close reasons), `evals/` (inventory, eval outputs, prototype files), `benchmarks/` (results, fixtures), `docs/`, the dist config and `.github/workflows/`. Ignored local files (`.beads/beads.db*`, `evals/out/`, `target/`) are not published and are out of scope, but confirm they are still ignored (`git status --ignored | head`).
- Step 1, scanners (outside the sandbox): `gitleaks version` (8.30.1 installed; `brew install gitleaks` if missing); `gitleaks git . --log-opts="--all" --redact -v --report-path "$TMPDIR/gl-git.json"` and `gitleaks dir . --redact -v --report-path "$TMPDIR/gl-dir.json"`; both must print "no leaks found". A finding that is a real credential value: record the file, commit and rule id only (never the value), do not fix by rewriting, go to Step 6.
- Step 2, manual pattern sweep over `git log --all -p` (read the matches, do not trust counts): `git log --all -p | grep -n -i -E "authorization:|bearer |sk-[a-z0-9]|ghp_|github_pat_|api[_-]?key=|token=|/Users/|/private/tmp/|/home/|claude\.ai/code/session|@gmail\.com|@[a-z0-9-]+\.(com|ai|io)"`; every hit is classified BENIGN (placeholder such as `TYPESAFE_API_KEY=test-key`, the commit author's own email in doc text, a public URL), PRIVATE (a local path, a session URL, a private repo or project name, personal tooling) or SECRET (a value). The commit author identity (name and email) on commits is Thomas's chosen public identity: BENIGN. Absolute paths inside internal files — bead descriptions, notes and close reasons, the plan, AGENTS.md (the checkout /Users/tpellet/Projects/hunch, the launch folder /Users/tpellet/Projects/hunch-launch/, the skill paths under /Users/tpellet/.claude/skills/) — are instructions: classify BENIGN-internal, no action. Only user-facing docs, code, benchmarks/, eval outputs and release artifacts must be free of them.
- Step 3, tracked-file review, one file at a time, by eye: README.md, PRIVACY.md, docs/ROBOT_MODE.md, CHANGELOG.md, benchmarks/README.md, benchmarks/results.md, evals/inventory.json (tool names from this machine are a light fingerprint: BENIGN, keep), evals/prototype/*, docs/superpowers/**, AGENTS.md, `.beads/issues.jsonl` (every `notes` and `close_reason`: no pasted API response, no draft sentence, no value), and every commit message body (`git log --format='%H%n%B' origin/main`). User-facing files (README.md, docs/ROBOT_MODE.md, PRIVACY.md, CHANGELOG.md, benchmarks/) must name the key path generically, `TYPESAFE_API_KEY_FILE=/path/to/key`, and describe the machine as "a typical macOS dev machine" (CPU/OS line allowed), and must carry no personal tooling details: no vault note titles, no `digital-double`/skill names, no reviewer model names, no per-machine tool counts such as "Thomas's Mac: 1,869 tools", no `~/.claude/` paths. Internal files (AGENTS.md, the plan, beads) may keep the real key path `$HOME/.ssh/typesafe-ai-key` and the tooling names. `grep -rn -E "typesafe-ai-key|Thomas's Mac|1,869|digital-double|\.claude/|Opus|Kimi" README.md PRIVACY.md docs/ROBOT_MODE.md CHANGELOG.md benchmarks/` must be empty (recursive: `bench.sh` and the fixtures are user-facing too).
- Step 4, launch drafts: `git ls-files | grep -i -E "launch|tweet|show-hn|announce"` must be empty and `ls docs/launch` must fail; `grep -n -i -E "show hn|tweet" .beads/issues.jsonl` may match only bead titles and the words of the rules (no draft sentence). Drafts live only in /Users/tpellet/Projects/hunch-launch/ (never listed, never read into the repo).
- Step 5, release surface: read the dist config (`dist-workspace.toml` or `[workspace.metadata.dist]`) and `.github/workflows/release.yml`; then build the installer locally without tagging, `dist build --artifacts=global` (or `dist build`; verify the flag against `dist build --help`), and `grep -n -E "/Users/|/private/tmp/|/home/[a-z]" target/distrib/*installer*.sh` must be empty; the only host in the script is github.com and the only `tpellet` is the repo path. Do not tag, do not push a tag.
- Step 6, findings. Fix-forward class (a local path or personal detail in a tracked file at HEAD, a stray private note in a bead field): fix it in this bead: each finding is its own fix-forward commit `fix: <what> (hunch-secret-pii-audit-8ha)` (keep `<what>` ≤ 22 characters) staging the fixed file and `.beads/issues.jsonl` carrying the tracker note (`br update hunch-secret-pii-audit-8ha --actor worker-<short-id> --append-notes "fixed forward: <file>, <class>"`, `br sync --flush-only`, no value), gated as usual and pushed after the pre-push scan; the close reason repeats "fixed forward: <file>, <class>" with the commit SHA. Rewrite/rotation class (a credential value anywhere in history, a private third-party detail in an old commit): do not rewrite, do not force-push, do not delete a tag; record "<class>, <file>, <commit>" in the close reason and with `br update hunch-v0-acceptance-xp2 --actor worker-<short-id> --append-notes "NOT ACCEPTED pending Thomas: <class, file, commit; no value>"`, `br sync --flush-only`, and leave THIS bead open so acceptance stays blocked; report it first in the hand-off. The lead's authorized history rewrite of 2026-09-19 removed the session trailers, the scratch path and an email line; the pre-code baseline is clean (17 commits at 5ed92d6), so any such item found now is a new finding.
- Step 7, close only after every step ran: the close reason is the pass/fail note: scanner results (commits scanned, leaks found), pattern-sweep classes with counts, files reviewed, launch-draft check, installer check, user-facing docs check, fix-forward commits (SHAs), and "no rewrite/rotation finding" or the blocking record.
- Rules (every bead): strictly serial on `main`, no branches/worktrees/PRs; gate and git with the sandbox disabled; never delete files; never read, print or copy ~/.ssh; treat unexplained working-tree changes as another agent's work: never stash, revert or overwrite them; commit only your own paths. Start with the CI pre-check (the "Before claiming" step of the CI criterion in Done when: a read-only `gh run list`; a red previous run is fixed and pushed under the previous bead's ID before anything else); only then claim: `br update hunch-secret-pii-audit-8ha --claim --actor worker-<short-id> --json` (pick a short id such as `worker-a1`; use the same `--actor` on every br command and name it in the close reason), then `br sync --flush-only`. `br` auto-flushes `.beads/issues.jsonl`: that file is yours to stage with your paths — the claim rides in your first commit (the first Step 6 `fix:` commit if there is one, else the close commit) and the close in the close commit (see Done when).

Files:
- Modify only on a fix-forward finding: the tracked file that carries the private detail (a user-facing doc, any file under benchmarks/, a code or eval file named in Steps 2–5), or a bead field through `br update`.
- Generated, not committed: `$TMPDIR/gl-git.json`, `$TMPDIR/gl-dir.json`, `target/distrib/`.
- Tracker: .beads/issues.jsonl (claim + close)

Prerequisites: hunch-task-16-release-ont (the dist config and README Install must exist). Blocks hunch-v0-acceptance-xp2.

Done when:
## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] `gitleaks git . --log-opts="--all"` and `gitleaks dir .` both printed "no leaks found" (or the finding is recorded by file, commit and rule id, never by value).
- [ ] The manual sweep and the per-file review ran over every tracked file, every bead note and close reason, and every commit body; each hit is classified; user-facing docs use `/path/to/key` and "a typical macOS dev machine" and the grep for personal tooling details is empty.
- [ ] No launch draft is tracked (`git ls-files` grep empty, no docs/launch/); the locally built installer script and the dist config carry no local path.
- [ ] Every fix-forward finding is fixed in a gated commit under this bead's ID; every rewrite/rotation finding is recorded (no value), v0 acceptance carries the NOT ACCEPTED note and this bead stays open. description:
Outcome: `hunch run` is complete: argument pointing from man-page flags and tokens copied from the request (`src/args.rs`), the never-execute list by tool name/prefix, `/dev/tty` confirmation or `--yes`, machine-mode execution only with `--exec --yes` (child stdout → stderr so stdout stays one envelope), and `hunch init zsh|bash` (the `,` alias); 5 contract + 3 unit tests pass; the live smoke `live_run_routes_tar` is added and run; committed and pushed.

The plan holds the verbatim, compile-verified code; copy it exactly, do not redesign. Run `cargo fmt` before `cargo fmt --check`.

Context:
- Consumes: Task 9 `cmd::run::{route, Route, RunFlags, load_tools}`; `manpage::{Flag, options_text, parse_flags}`, `inventory::Tool` (Task 8); `jev::client::Client`, `jev::{Question, Questions}`, `Response.answers` (Tasks 2–3); `cmd::confirm_tty` (Task 1, the shared prompt), `cli::Shell`, `cmd::Outcome`, `Exit`, `HunchError::{Declined, Input}`; `tests/live.rs::live_key_present` (Task 8); harness `common::{mock, hunch, bin, FakeJev, option_containing}`.

Read first: ~/.claude/AGENTS.md and /Users/tpellet/Projects/hunch/AGENTS.md (every time); the spec docs/superpowers/specs/2026-09-18-hunch-v0-design.md; the plan docs/superpowers/plans/2026-09-18-hunch-v0.md — "## Global Constraints", the section "#### Task 13c: Demo" (Steps 1–2) and Task 12 Step 3 (latency claims rule: the demo must not show or claim a latency that is not in benchmarks/results.md — the `-v` timing lines it prints are raw output, fine).

Context:
- Needs the release binary (`cargo build --release`; use `./target/release/hunch` or install it on PATH for the recording), `vhs` (`brew install vhs` if absent) and the live key: run the recording as `TYPESAFE_API_KEY_FILE=$HOME/.ssh/typesafe-ai-key vhs demo.tape` with the sandbox disabled. hunch reads the key; you never read, print or echo it, and the GIF must not show the key or the variable's value — pass it through the environment of the vhs process, never on a typed command line inside the tape.
- Live-step policy: the recording is expected to happen — the key file exists on this machine. Only if the live calls genuinely fail (network or API down, retried once) may the bead close without the GIF: commit demo.tape and the fixtures, record the exact error with `br update hunch-task-13c-demo-jk1 --actor worker-<short-id> --append-notes "NOT RUN: vhs recording — <error>"`, create a follow-up bead (`br create --title "Record demo.gif (hunch-task-13c-demo-jk1)" -t task -p 1 -l live,v0 --description "<the vhs command, the five scenes, review by Thomas>" --json`, then `br dep add hunch-v0-acceptance-xp2 <new-id>`), and say NOT RUN in the close reason; no GIF is committed in that case.
- Record, in this order, each with `-v` so cost/time show on stderr: (1) `hunch why -- cargo build` inside a fixture crate whose first error is buried under ~300 warnings; (2) `ls fixtures/downloads | hunch pick "last month's electricity bill"` over a fixture directory with invented file names; (3) `hunch is "asks for a refund" < mail.txt; echo $?`; (4) `, burn a dvd from this iso` (a proposal, declined at the prompt with `n`); (5) `, make a qr code` (abstain, exit 3). Output `demo.gif` at the repo root (README from 13b references it; replace the placeholder line if 13b used one).
- Fixtures live under benchmarks/fixtures/demo/ (the failing crate with its own Cargo.toml, `fixtures/downloads/` file names, `mail.txt`, an empty placeholder `.iso` name). The fixture crate must fail to build by design. Cargo never compiles a nested crate as a target of the root package, so no root Cargo.toml edit is needed (`[package] exclude` only affects packaging and is not the mechanism); instead give the fixture crate its own empty `[workspace]` table in its Cargo.toml so it never joins a root workspace (Task 16's `dist init` may add one to the root Cargo.toml, and a nested crate without its own `[workspace]` then stops building with "believes it's in a workspace"). Running `hunch why -- cargo build` inside the fixture creates `benchmarks/fixtures/demo/<crate>/target/`, which the root-anchored `/target` ignore does not cover: append `benchmarks/fixtures/demo/**/target/` to `.gitignore` and stage the fixture sources explicitly, never a `target/` directory (check `git status` before committing). Verify `cargo check --all-targets` and `cargo test -- --test-threads=1` at the root still pass with the fixtures present.
- Thomas reviews the GIF before publish: commit and push it (the repo is where he sees it), and state in the close reason and hand-off that demo.gif awaits his review.
- Rules (every bead): strictly serial on `main`, no branches/worktrees/PRs; gate and git with the sandbox disabled; never delete files; never read/print ~/.ssh; treat unexplained working-tree changes as another agent's work: never stash, revert or overwrite them; commit only your own paths. - Create: demo.tape, demo.gif, benchmarks/fixtures/demo/** (fixture crate with its own `[workspace]`, fixtures/downloads listing, mail.txt, iso placeholder)
- Modify: .gitignore (append `benchmarks/fixtures/demo/**/target/`); README.md only if the GIF placeholder line needs replacing
- Tracker: .beads/issues.jsonl (claim + close)
- Never: the root Cargo.toml (not needed for this bead)

Prerequisites: hunch-task-13b-readme-4vz

Done when:
## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] demo.gif exists, produced by `vhs demo.tape` with the live key (or NOT RUN per the live-step policy: follow-up bead created, no GIF committed), shows the five scenes in order, and contains no key material or personal paths.
- [ ] Gate green with the fixtures present (sandbox disabled): `cargo fmt --check && cargo check --all-targets && cargo clippy --all-targets -- -D warnings && cargo test -- --test-threads=1`; `ubs demo.tape .gitignore` (plus README.md if changed), run outside the sandbox (ubs creates its temp dir under /var/folders). ubs scans only the languages it supports (.rs, .py, …): this bead changes none (the fixture crate's .rs files are fixtures, not hunch code — do not add them to make ubs scan), so ubs exits 3 "nothing scanned" — that is expected, not a failure: record `ubs: not applicable — nothing scanned (exit 3)` in the close reason; never set `UBS_ALLOW_NO_SCAN` or any override. - [ ] `git status` shows no `target/` directory under benchmarks/fixtures/demo/ as untracked or staged.
- [ ] Close before committing, once the gate passed: `br close hunch-task-13c-demo-jk1 --actor worker-<short-id> --reason "<scenes recorded, awaiting Thomas's review of demo.gif, ubs warnings left, CI conclusion of the previous push (the filtered gh run list of the CI criterion matched on the origin/main SHA, outside the sandbox; a red run there was fixed under its own bead's ID before you claimed; if gh is unavailable, say so)>" --json`, then `br sync --flush-only`.

State `pre-push scan: clean` in the hand-off.
- [ ] CI (one rule for every bead: a red run belongs to the bead whose push turned it red and is fixed under that bead's ID). title: wave-2 acceptance: live add/sort check, gate, push
description:
Outcome: Wave 2 is verified live and published: `hunch add` and `hunch sort` exercised on real temporary data with the real key, every contract surface (help, capabilities, robot-docs, README, PRIVACY, CHANGELOG) lists both verbs consistently, the full gate is green, and `origin main` is pushed. Tagging a new release is Thomas's call. This bead is lead-added, not in the plan: the plan's execution order ends at Task 15 and names no wave-2 acceptance pass or CHANGELOG entry; this bead fills that gap on the v0-acceptance pattern.

Read first: ~/.claude/AGENTS.md and /Users/tpellet/Projects/hunch/AGENTS.md (every time); the plan docs/superpowers/plans/2026-09-18-hunch-v0.md — "## Global Constraints", "## CUT LINE — v0 is public before anything below starts", "### Task 14 (wave 2): `hunch add` — stage hunks by topic", "### Task 15 (wave 2): `hunch sort` — files into existing folders, dry-run first"; README.md, docs/ROBOT_MODE.md, PRIVACY.md, CHANGELOG.md as shipped.

Context:
- Live checks — sandbox DISABLED, `TYPESAFE_API_KEY_FILE=$HOME/.ssh/typesafe-ai-key` in each command's environment (hunch reads the file; never read, print or echo it). These are expected to run: the key file exists on this machine. `cargo build --release`; `H=$PWD/target/release/hunch`. Record exit code + one-line output + observed effect for each:
  - add: in a throwaway git repo under $TMPDIR (`git init -q`, `git config commit.gpgsign false`, user.name/email set locally, one committed 40-line file, then two unrelated working-tree edits: an "AUTH fix" line and a "typo" line): `$H add --dry-run "the auth fix"` → 0, table of hunks with p; `$H --json add "the auth fix"` → 130, `git diff --cached` empty; `$H add --yes "the auth fix"` → 0, `git diff --cached` shows only the AUTH hunk; from a subdirectory of that repo `$H add --yes "anything"` still stages the top-level file; with a clean tree `$H add --yes "anything"` → 6.
  - sort: a temp dir with folders Finance/ and Poems/ and files march.txt ("invoice total 42 EUR") and poem.txt ("roses are red"): `$H --json sort <dir>` → dry-run, ≥ 1 move proposed, nothing moved; `$H --json sort <dir> --apply` → files moved, `data.undo_log` is a path; `$H sort <dir> --undo <log>` → files back, exit 0; `$H sort <dir> --into /nonexistent` → 6; `$H sort <empty dir>` → 6.
  - Contract: `$H --help` lists add and sort; `$H capabilities --json` lists both with exit codes and data; `$H robot-docs guide` mentions both; PRIVACY.md has both rows; README has both sections; `cargo test -- --test-threads=1` green.
  Two kinds of check, two rules (same lead decision as hunch-v0-acceptance-xp2). Deterministic contract checks — a clean tree → 6, `--into /nonexistent` → 6, an empty dir → 6, dry-run moves nothing, `--json add` without `--yes` stages nothing (`git diff --cached` empty), undo restores what `--apply` moved and never overwrites a taken original path, the envelope shape, the test suite, and help/capabilities/robot-docs/README/PRIVACY/CHANGELOG listing both verbs — must pass; a failure is a code defect: fix in place (gate, commit `fix: <what> (hunch-wave2-acceptance-non)`, `<what>` ≤ 22 characters) or report NOT ACCEPTED with the evidence and leave the bead open. Model-judgment checks — which hunks `add` picks for a topic (zero chosen → exit 3, and the 130 decline check is then unreachable, which is a miss, not a decline-path defect) and whether `sort` proposes and makes the expected moves — get exactly one re-run with `--no-cache`; a persistent miss is recorded verbatim (command, exit code, output) in the close reason and with `br update hunch-wave2-acceptance-non --actor worker-<short-id> --append-notes "<miss>"`; it does not block acceptance. Never change prompts, constants or the threshold to "fix" one example. Only if every model-judgment check misses is it a code defect (the pipeline, not the model): investigate, fix in place or NOT ACCEPTED. If the API or network is down, append the error with `br update hunch-wave2-acceptance-non --actor worker-<short-id> --append-notes "<error>"`, leave the bead open and stop; retry later.
- CHANGELOG.md: add an "Unreleased" entry (or the next version's, if Thomas named one) listing `add` and `sort` with their safety rules (index only / dry-run by default, never overwrites, never deletes).
- Full gate (sandbox disabled): `cargo fmt --check && cargo check --all-targets && cargo clippy --all-targets -- -D warnings && cargo test -- --test-threads=1`; `ubs CHANGELOG.md` plus any changed files, outside the sandbox: if none of them is a language ubs scans (.rs, .py, …), ubs exits 3 "nothing scanned" — expected, not a failure: record `ubs: not applicable — nothing scanned (exit 3)` in the close reason; never set `UBS_ALLOW_NO_SCAN` or any override, never touch a code file to make it scan; if it scanned something, exit 0 is the bar: fix genuine bugs at the root and give the warning count by category in the close reason.
- Full-history rescan before closing (public repo; the per-push scan below covers each push, this covers everything wave 2 added): `gitleaks git . --log-opts="--all" --redact -v` must print "no leaks found", and `git log v0.1.0..HEAD -p` (or `origin/main~N..HEAD` for the wave-2 commits if no tag exists) is read by eye for the same private-information list as the pre-push scan; record `full-history rescan: clean` in the close reason, or the fix-forward commit that cleaned it (no values quoted).
- Publish: `git pull --rebase` if needed; `git push origin main` (sandbox disabled); `git status` shows up to date. Do not tag unless Thomas asked for a release; state that in the hand-off.
- Rules: no branches; never delete files; treat unexplained working-tree changes as another agent's work: never stash, revert or overwrite them; commit only your own paths. Start with the CI pre-check (the "Before claiming" step of the CI criterion in Done when: a read-only `gh run list`; a red previous run is fixed and pushed under the previous bead's ID before anything else); only then claim: `br update hunch-wave2-acceptance-non --claim --actor worker-<short-id> --json` (pick a short id such as `worker-a1`; use the same `--actor` on every br command and name it in the close reason), then `br sync --flush-only`. `br` auto-flushes `.beads/issues.jsonl`: that file is yours to stage with your paths — the claim and the close ride in this bead's one commit (see Done when).

Files: CHANGELOG.md; fixes only where the live checks reveal a defect; tracker .beads/issues.jsonl (claim + close).

Prerequisites: hunch-task-15-sort-s0w

Done when:
## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] Every live add/sort command above ran with the recorded exit code and observed effect (staged hunks, moved and restored files): every deterministic check passed; each model-judgment miss (if any) was re-run once with `--no-cache` and is recorded in the notes and the close reason.
- [ ] help, capabilities, robot-docs, README, PRIVACY and CHANGELOG list both wave-2 verbs consistently.
- [ ] Full gate green; `ubs` exit 0 on the changed files it scans, or `ubs: not applicable — nothing scanned (exit 3)` recorded.
- [ ] Full-history rescan ran (`gitleaks git . --log-opts="--all"` clean, wave-2 commits read by eye); `full-history rescan: clean` is in the close reason.
- [ ] Close before committing, once everything above passed: `br close hunch-wave2-acceptance-non --actor worker-<short-id> --reason "<commands with exit codes, full-history rescan result, ubs warnings left, CI conclusion of the previous push (the filtered gh run list of the CI criterion matched on the origin/main SHA, outside the sandbox; a red run there was fixed under its own bead's ID before you claimed; if gh is unavailable, say so)>" --json`; `br sync --flush-only`.
- [ ] One signed commit: `git add CHANGELOG.md .beads/issues.jsonl`; subject `docs: changelog for wave-2 verbs (hunch-wave2-acceptance-non)`; `git push origin main` (sandbox disabled; if rejected, `git pull --rebase`, never stash or force-push); `git status` shows up to date with origin/main; no tag created unless Thomas asked.
- [ ] Pre-push scan (every bead: the repo `tpellet/hunch` is public, so a push is publication; the rule is ~/.claude/AGENTS.md "## Public Repositories — Push With Care", this is the hunch form). Before every `git push`, outside the sandbox: `gitleaks git . --log-opts="origin/main..HEAD" --redact -v` (gitleaks 8.30.1 is installed; `brew install gitleaks` if it is missing; the repo's `.gitleaks.toml` allowlist, added by hunch-task-01-scaffold-p8n, is picked up automatically) must end with "no leaks found"; then read `git diff origin/main..HEAD` yourself for private information: API keys or tokens, `Authorization` headers, pasted API responses, emails other than the commit author's, absolute local paths (`/Users/...`, `/private/tmp/...`) anywhere but in bead and plan instructions, which already name the checkout and the launch folder by absolute path, scratchpad or session URLs, names of Thomas's private repos or projects, personal or admin details, other people's data, communications drafts (tweet, Show HN, announcement: those live only in /Users/tpellet/Projects/hunch-launch/, never in the repo, bead notes, close reasons or commit messages). User-facing files (README.md, docs/ROBOT_MODE.md, PRIVACY.md, CHANGELOG.md, benchmarks/) name the key path generically, `TYPESAFE_API_KEY_FILE=/path/to/key`, and the machine as "a typical macOS dev machine": never the real key file name, never tool counts of Thomas's Mac, never his personal tooling (vault notes, skills, reviewer models); internal files (AGENTS.md, the plan, beads) may keep the real key path. Any hit: do not push; fix forward in a new commit under this bead's ID (never rewrite history, never force-push), `br update hunch-wave2-acceptance-non --actor worker-<short-id> --append-notes "pre-push: <what was removed, no values>"`, `br sync --flush-only`, re-scan, then push. A secret that already reached the remote: stop, do not rewrite, report it in the hand-off (Thomas rotates the key). Commit bodies stay technical: no `Co-Authored-By`, no `Claude-Session:` trailer (whether that trailer counts as private is an open question for Thomas; until he answers, leave it out). State `pre-push scan: clean` in the hand-off.
- [ ] CI (one rule for every bead: a red run belongs to the bead whose push turned it red and is fixed under that bead's ID). Before claiming — the first step of this bead, read-only: `gh run list --workflow ci.yml --branch main --limit 3 --json databaseId,headSha,status,conclusion` (outside the sandbox) and use the run whose `headSha` equals `git rev-parse origin/main` (re-list after a few seconds if it is not there yet). If that run is red, fix it under the previous bead's ID before you claim: first `br update <previous-bead-id> --actor worker-<short-id> --append-notes "CI fix: <what>"` and `br sync --flush-only`, then one commit `fix: <what> (<previous-bead-id>)` staging the fix and `.beads/issues.jsonl` (gate, push; report the fix SHA in the hand-off); only then claim this bead. After your push: the same `gh run list`, using the run whose `headSha` equals `git rev-parse HEAD`, then `gh run watch <databaseId>` until it ends; report the conclusion in the hand-off; a red run is noted first with `br update hunch-wave2-acceptance-non --actor worker-<short-id> --append-notes "CI fix: <what>"` and `br sync --flush-only`, then fixed in a follow-up commit `fix: <what> (hunch-wave2-acceptance-non)` staging the fix and `.beads/issues.jsonl` (gate, push; report the fix SHA in the hand-off) before your session ends. Fix subjects: keep `<what>` ≤ 22 characters so the subject stays < 72 (check with `git log -1 --format=%s | awk '{print length}'`). A red run your Mac cannot reproduce (Linux-only, or a toolchain difference — CI pins `dtolnay/rust-toolchain@1.93.1`, the toolchain the plan was verified on; keep it pinned) is fixed the same way under this rule: read `gh run view <databaseId> --log-failed`, fix the cause at the root or the CI environment (e.g. a missing package in `ci.yml`); never `#[ignore]`, `#[cfg]`-gate or delete a test, never loosen a workflow check, and `#[allow]` only a demonstrable false positive, with a one-line comment. Release-workflow (tag) runs belong to the acceptance bead, not to this rule. If `gh` is unavailable, say so in the close reason.
